feed.title: NPR Topics: Science
feed.subtitle: The latest health and science news. Updates on medicine, healthy living, nutrition, drugs, diet, and advances in science and technology. Subscribe to the Health & Science podcast.

entry.title: What the equinox 'henge' effect tells us about U.S. cities
entry.summary: The fall equinox, which arrives Tuesday in the U.S., brings shorter days, and chances to witness alignment between Earth and the sun. It's a modern version of ancient observances of a celestial shift.

entry.title: This farm raised thousands of pigs for slaughter. Now it's growing mushrooms instead
entry.summary: The U.S. gets nearly a third of its pork from Iowa. One family is making the switch from pigs to more sustainable specialty mushrooms and trying to show other pig farmers how they did it.

entry.title: Poison suspected in deaths of ten lions in game reserve in Tanzania
entry.summary: The lions were found dead inside the Ngorongoro Conservation Area, a popular wildlife reserve in Tanzania. Deaths raise concerns over wildlife poisonings in East Africa.

entry.title: Monarch butterflies are on their way to Mexico. States are helping them on their way
entry.summary: Eastern monarch butterflies are flying more than 2,000 miles south, through the central U.S., to overwinter in Mexico. We look at a project aimed to help the pollinators along their journey.

entry.title: SpaceX has big plans for a new Louisiana 'Star Base,' worrying some near there
entry.summary: State officials say the new SpaceX site will be a $100 billion investment and launch thousands of rockets. Lawmakers helped ease regulations and negotiations were covered under nondisclosure agreements.

entry.title: Archaeologists are racing to save precious artifacts in Alaska after last year's storm
entry.summary: Last year, remnants of a typhoon damaged homes, infrastructure and an archaeological dig site. Now, archaeologists are trying to get as many objects out as possible before the next storm.

entry.title: Alaska's salmon-feasting bears face off in biggest Fat Bear Week ever
entry.summary: This year's single-elimination tournament will see 16 competitors face off, compared to 12 in past years. Officials report more cubs in Katmai National Park than they've seen in recent memory.

entry.title: Could trees developed with gene-editing technology protect Florida's citrus industry?
entry.summary: A bacterial infection is wiping out Florida's citrus trees. Growers hope a rootstock developed with gene-editing technology could keep the disease at bay.

entry.title: This week in science: T. rex footprints, solar 'superflares,' and benefits of reading
entry.summary: Paleontologists have discovered the tracks of a giant — the fossilized footprints of T. rex. Plus, solar "superflares" and the brain benefits of reading in this week's Short Wave science news roundup.

entry.title: Why reshaping memories may hold the key to raising self-esteem
entry.summary: In a new book, psychologist Marisa Franco explains why it's good to feel good about yourself — and shares a helpful memory technique that we've turned into a printable worksheet.
